# Certificate Based Courses

Duration: 4 months / 16 teaching weeks.
Schedule: 6 instructor-led hours weekly (96 total), plus 4 to 6 independent study hours.

Prepare students for one selected vendor credential through objective mapping, applied labs, knowledge checks, scenario reasoning, and targeted revision. Each cohort follows one credential route rather than attempting all credentials simultaneously.

## Prerequisites

Entry requirements depend on the route. Complete the related technical course or pass a practical placement assessment before joining an associate-level route.

## Tools

Official Microsoft Learn or AWS learning resources; vendor practice assessments; approved lab environments; instructor-created original exercises.

## Learning outcomes

- Map personal skills and learning gaps to the selected official exam objectives.
- Complete practical scenarios demonstrating the skills behind exam questions.
- Explain architectural or analytical choices and eliminate unsuitable alternatives.
- Create an evidence-based readiness plan using practice results and demonstrated skills.

## Weekly schedule

### Week 1 — Orientation and diagnostic

Choose one credential; review current objectives, format and policies.

Practical: Complete a diagnostic and create a personal learning plan.

### Week 2 — Domain one foundations

Core concepts and terminology for the selected route.

Practical: Map foundational concepts to an applied scenario.

### Week 3 — Domain one practice

Configuration, use cases and common misconceptions.

Practical: Complete a graded foundational lab.

### Week 4 — Domain two foundations

Second objective group and dependencies.

Practical: Explain a design or analytical decision from a scenario.

### Week 5 — Domain two practice

Implementation, testing and troubleshooting.

Practical: Complete a second graded lab with evidence.

### Week 6 — Domain three foundations

Third objective group and integration points.

Practical: Build a concept map linked to official objectives.

### Week 7 — Domain three practice

Multi-step scenarios and performance or quality tradeoffs.

Practical: Complete an integrated lab and defend choices.

### Week 8 — Midpoint readiness review

Objective coverage, cumulative practical and gap analysis.

Practical: Update the learning plan using demonstrated weaknesses.

### Week 9 — Remaining objective groups

Route-specific objectives not yet covered; security and governance.

Practical: Complete missing objective labs.

### Week 10 — Integrated scenarios

Cross-domain architecture, modeling or pipeline reasoning.

Practical: Resolve a realistic end-to-end case.

### Week 11 — Troubleshooting and operations

Failure diagnosis, monitoring, access and lifecycle management.

Practical: Investigate a broken configuration or analytical workflow.

### Week 12 — Practical portfolio

Consolidate evidence and document repeatable steps.

Practical: Submit a complete objective-to-evidence matrix.

### Week 13 — Timed mock one

Original questions, scenario pacing and answer justification.

Practical: Record domain-level results and categorize mistakes.

### Week 14 — Targeted remediation

Weak domains, repeated misconceptions and skills reinforcement.

Practical: Retest missed skills with new questions and labs.

### Week 15 — Timed mock two

Fresh original assessment and practical readiness review.

Practical: Compare results and justify an exam readiness decision.

### Week 16 — Final readiness and next steps

Revision plan, registration steps and continued learning.

Practical: Present the portfolio and personal exam preparation plan.

## Capstone

Credential aligned practical portfolio and readiness review

Submit an objective-to-evidence matrix, lab portfolio, error log, two original timed mock assessments, targeted revision plan, and practical demonstration. Vendor exam registration and fees are separate.

## Assessment

- Weekly practical work: 25%
- Knowledge checks: 10%
- Midpoint practical: 20%
- Capstone artifact: 35%
- Presentation and defense: 10%
